stem: A client who has smoked for many years says, 'At my age, quitting probably would not help much.' Which response by the nurse is accurate?

options.A: Health benefits occur only after at least 10 years of abstinence
options.B: Benefits begin soon after the last cigarette and quitting improves health at any age
options.C: Quitting provides meaningful benefit mainly to younger people with a short smoking history
options.D: Once cardiovascular disease is present, stopping smoking no longer reduces cardiovascular risk

rationale: CDC states that quitting smoking has health benefits at any age regardless of how long or how much a person has smoked. Positive changes begin after the last cigarette: heart rate drops within minutes, nicotine in the blood reaches zero by 24 hours, and carbon monoxide falls over the next several days, with additional cardiovascular and other benefits accumulating over time. Therefore B is correct. A and C wrongly delay or restrict benefit, and D conflicts with CDC guidance that people with coronary heart disease also benefit from quitting.
educational_objective: Teach that smoking cessation produces health benefits at any age and that beneficial physiologic changes begin soon after the last cigarette and continue over time.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Sections 'Health benefits of quitting smoking' and 'Health benefits of quitting smoking over time' — benefits at any age; heart rate drops within minutes; nicotine reaches zero by 24 hours; carbon monoxide falls over several days; cardiovascular risk continues to decline
source_claim_supported: Smoking cessation benefits health regardless of age or smoking duration, with physiologic benefits beginning soon after the last cigarette and continuing over time.
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, Appendix A printed p.28 / PDF p.31, Health Promotion/Disease Prevention: 'Educate client on actions to promote and maintain health and prevent disease (e.g., smoking cessation, diet, weight loss)'
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — smoking cessation / disease prevention
correction_summary: Replaced the vague 'within hours to days' statement with the directly supported counseling principle that benefits begin soon after the last cigarette and occur at any age. Rebuilt the stem as a realistic client-teaching scenario, removed cue-heavy distractors, and pinned the exact NCSBN smoking-cessation blueprint statement.
audit_findings: B is directly supported by CDC. A falsely delays benefit for a decade, C falsely restricts benefit by age/smoking duration, and D conflicts with documented benefit in people with coronary heart disease. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
